body.text: FISH NEWS EXCLUSIVE: New Door Installed At RAF Cranwell Officers' Mess, Sources Confirm It Does, In Fact, Open

In what insiders are already calling a watershed moment for base infrastructure, RAF Cranwell can confirm the installation of a new door into the Officers' Mess, replacing what witnesses describe only as "the previous door."

The door, described by engineering staff as "structurally a door" and "technically successful" in its primary function of separating one space from another, was fitted following what Fish News understands to have been a lengthy and largely uneventful procurement process.

"We're calling it a significant upgrade to base morale," said one duty officer, who did not elaborate on what the previous door had done to morale, or indeed whether morale had been consulted at any stage. "It opens. It closes. Frankly, we're thrilled."

A junior technician present during installation, speaking on condition of anonymity despite being stood directly beneath a sign bearing his name and rank, told Fish News the door had been "hung correctly, as far as anyone can tell," and that early reports of a slight draught were "under review, but not currently a priority."
When asked whether the new door represented an improvement over its predecessor, the Mess's catering officer offered only: "It is a door. I have seen it. It was there this morning."

Fish News understands the old door has been decommissioned and its current whereabouts remain unclear, though rumours of a quiet burial ceremony attended by three officers and a dog have not been officially confirmed or denied.

Chunce Whatney, filing this report from what he insists was "the exact same doorway used to smuggle intelligence out of Constantinople," declined to comment further on the door itself, noting only that he had "seen ten thousand doors close on ten thousand empires" and that this one, comparatively, "hinges rather well."
Fish News will continue to monitor the door, as is our solemn duty, for as long as it remains a door.
